import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_95/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_95/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_95/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on movie_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0[['movie_id', 'title']], source1, on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Join the above result with Source2 on user_id
join_all = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2[['user_id', 'sex']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Group by movie_id and title, pivot on sex to get average rating per sex as columns F and M
pivot = join_all.groupby(['movie_id', 'title', 'sex'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()
pivot_table = pivot.pivot(index=['movie_id', 'title'], columns='sex', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot_table = pivot_table.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Ensure columns exist for both 'F' and 'M' (if any sex missing, fill with NaN)
if 'F' not in pivot_table.columns:
    pivot_table['F'] = pd.NA
if 'M' not in pivot_table.columns:
    pivot_table['M'] = pd.NA

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target3_95 = pivot_table[['movie_id', 'title', 'F', 'M']]

# Convert movie_id to integer type explicitly
target3_95['movie_id'] = target3_95['movie_id'].astype(int)

# Save the final target table to the specified path
target3_95.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_95_1 and Source3_95_2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source3_95_0 and the above join on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Pivot table to get average rating grouped by movie_id, title and sex, pivot sex into columns F and M
pivot = (
    joined_all.groupby(["movie_id", "title", "sex"])["rating"]
    .mean()
    .unstack(level=-1)
    .rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M"})
    .reset_index()
)

# The pivot columns might have missing values for some sex groups, keep as is (NaN)
# Ensure columns are exactly as target schema
pivot = pivot[["movie_id", "title", "F", "M"]]

# Write output
pivot.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_95/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
